story.headline: Microsoft asks the public to help shape its future AI rules.

heroVisual.alt: An illustrated draft sheet, fountain pen and coloured comment slips on a desk.

story.the_story:
Microsoft AI opened a six-week public consultation on September 14 about how its future MAI models should behave. A model is the trained component that produces AI outputs; MAI means the models developed by Microsoft AI, not every model or product Microsoft offers.

The draft Humanist AI Code of Conduct is not being used to train models today. Microsoft plans a revised version later in 2026 to guide development from 2027 onward.
story.laidies_read:
The proposed rules say MAI models should accept interruption, correction and shutdown, and stay within the work people authorize. Imagine asking an AI to prepare a message, then cancelling. The proposed principle is that it should stop through any predefined safe-stopping procedure, rather than make your intervention harder or restart without permission.

Publishing that rule makes the intention inspectable. It does not show that a model reliably follows it. Microsoft acknowledges that gap: written objectives cannot ensure the intended behavior, and building, testing and revision remain necessary.
story.what_this_means:
This is an invitation to comment, not a current account or settings change. Microsoft welcomes views from the general public as well as researchers and governments. You can flag a particular passage or question the overall approach.

If you want to contribute, choose one situation you know well: what should an AI do when you say “stop”? Read the relevant draft passage, describe where it is unclear or misses your situation, and use Microsoft’s linked feedback form. That question is a starting point, not a required submission format.

Microsoft plans to report what it learned and changed, but does not promise to incorporate each suggestion. You do not need to arrive as an AI expert to bring a concrete concern.
story.cocktail_party: “Microsoft is asking people to comment on rules for future MAI models. A written promise is something to inspect—not proof that today’s AI already behaves that way.”
story.class_notes: AI Fundamentals 101: From “Whatever” to “RSVP: Yes. I have notes.” explains why understanding AI helps you participate in decisions about its future.

universalAnswers.whatHappened: Microsoft opened a six-week consultation on a first draft AI behavior code September 14.
universalAnswers.plainLanguageIdentity: A model is the trained component producing outputs; MAI denotes Microsoft AI-developed models.
universalAnswers.evidenceBasis: Official announcement and complete draft captured September 15 support the invitation, intended rules and limits.
universalAnswers.evidenceLimits: Written objectives are not present performance evidence or complete deployment safeguards.
universalAnswers.readerRelevance: Readers can contribute a concrete concern before future guidance is revised.
universalAnswers.affectedPeople: General public, Users and Operators, researchers, governments and Microsoft AI training teams are named audiences.
universalAnswers.changesNow: The consultation is open; the draft is not used for training today and no current account change is announced.
universalAnswers.uncertainty: Final wording and which feedback is incorporated remain undecided.
universalAnswers.readerAction: Read one relevant passage and describe a stopping situation using the official linked form.
universalAnswers.betterQuestion: What would a safe stop mean in a situation I know?

legal-policy.legalStatus: A voluntary provider draft consultation, not legislation, a court judgment or an enacted product requirement.
legal-policy.jurisdiction: Scope is Microsoft AI-developed MAI models, not models merely hosted or used by Microsoft.
legal-policy.parties: Microsoft AI authors and revises; public respondents can offer views without guaranteed incorporation.
legal-policy.allegationVsFinding: Microsoft states intended future behavior; the draft expressly acknowledges a gap from actual model behavior.
legal-policy.currentEffect: Public feedback can be submitted now; no present settings instruction is supported.
legal-policy.unresolvedQuestions: Revised text, implementation and measured adherence remain to be established.
legal-policy.nextMilestone: Consultation closes after six weeks; Microsoft plans a learned/changed summary and revised code later in 2026.
